children: rallied in early trading on Wednesday after battling through consumer spending to post 3.1% revenue growth and adjusted net income growth of 11.6%.

"While consumer spending remains pressured, particularly among lower-income households, our team has continued to execute at a high level by focusing on the key events and categories that matter most to our customers," highlighted CEO Steve Lawrence. "We are reinvesting tariff-related benefits into value, expanding compelling new brands and categories, and accelerating initiatives across stores, omni-channel, and loyalty," he added. The retailer noted it is gaining market share and strengthening customer engagement, which reinforces its confidence in achieving FY26 sales and earnings objectives.
On the development front, Academy Sports

opened three new stores during the second quarter, bringing its total to 327 locations. The company plans to open eleven stores during the third quarter, with the remaining locations to be opened in the fourth quarter of FY26.
Shares of Academy Sports and Outdoors
shot up 10.7% in premarket trading to $49.50 vs. the 52-week range of $41.29 to $62.45. Short interest on ASO stands at 12.3% of the total float.

title: Academy Sports rallies after battling through consumer spending headwinds
